_comment: Per-environment flash budget, in bytes, checked by tools/check_flash_budget.py.
The number compared is the one PlatformIO itself prints ('Flash: ... used N
bytes from M bytes'), not a size computed here — a gate that reimplements the
measurement is a gate that can disagree with what the developer sees.
A budget is a HIGH-WATER MARK, not the linker ceiling. The linker already
refuses an image that does not fit; what it cannot do is make growth visible
while there is still room. Each budget sits a few KB above the measured size
at the time it was set, so ordinary work passes and a jump has to be paid for
by editing this file in the same change — which puts the number in the diff,
where a reviewer sees it.
Raising a budget is a normal thing to do. Raising it without saying why in the
commit message is not.
'headroom' is documentation, not enforcement: measured - budget is what the
gate allows; ceiling - measured is what the hardware allows. Note the ceiling
reported by PlatformIO is the program slot alone and says nothing about the
LittleFS partition behind it (see docs/ANALISE_FLASH_RAM.md).
2026-09-09: 'used' is the SUM OF SECTIONS and understates the footprint. The
linker aligns .data's load address to 4 KiB, so the .bin (what the slot
actually holds) is larger by the padding: pico_w_air 1,025,600 used vs a
1,039,508 B .bin, 4,972 B of real slack. Real slack moves in 4 KiB steps -
readelf -l firmware.elf, end of the last LOAD in flash, is the number.
2026-09-11 (feat/fleet-api): the OTA-safe ceiling is 1,040,384 B of .bin (1016 KiB,
OTA_APP_SAFE_MAX_SIZE), not the 1,044,480 program slot: the last 4 KiB sector of
the slot is where the config snapshot lands at stage time. pico_w_air's .bin is
1,039,508 B on main AND on this branch - 876 B of real OTA slack, not 4,972.
The Air budget margin is 1,000 B for that reason; every future byte there is a trade.
2026-09-18 (feat/screen-mirror): the three TFT budgets go up because the panel
mirror landed - /api/screen_stream, its palette-RLE codec, POST /api/touch and the
dashboard canvas that drives them. release 1,024,340 -> 1,027,852, test +3,408,
asserts +3,528; the margin stays the 3,000 B this file has always used. alpha and
air keep their old budgets: neither has a panel, so both carry only the ~1.5 kB of
gzipped page, and both still fit.
2026-09-19 (study/core1-pause-mirror): 'measured' moves up and the budgets do
NOT. The panel mirror's Core-1 pause became a park without the SDK lockout, and
Core 1 idles for the length of a capture: +816 B on release, +968 on test,
+56 on alpha and +8 on air - the two imageless builds carry only the microsecond
stamps. Every environment is still inside the 3,000 B margin this file has
always used, so nothing here had to be raised; what would have been dishonest is
leaving 'measured' describing an image that no longer exists.
2026-09-19 (second pass): the budgets for the four panel builds GO UP, and this
is the raise the rule asks to be argued for. The mirror gained a DMA read
pipeline, a send-coalescing buffer and a second wire codec: +2,048 B on release,
and the 3,000 B margin this file has always carried had fallen to 136 B - on
pico_w_test it went 32 B negative, which is the gate doing its job. Budgets are
reset to measured + 3,000 so the next ordinary change is not blocked by a margin
that quietly ran out. alpha and air move by 16 and 8 B (a constexpr and a header
they barely touch) and keep their own margins, 2,928 and 1,000.
2026-09-19 (feat/alarms-live-config): +2,896 B on release, +6,352 on alpha,
+2,208 on air. Three things: a per-slot maintenance window (CONFIG_VERSION 23,
tail-append), a third payload domain in the alarm line, and ConfigApply.h -
which classifies what a commit changed so the handler reboots only for what
needs it. ConfigApply started as thirty hand-written compare/copy functions and
cost 4,488 B; rewritten as one span table walked by one loop it costs 2,896 and
the two halves can no longer drift apart. Budgets go to measured + 3,000 (air
keeps its 1,000); the air .bin is 1,027,116 B, 13,268 under the OTA ceiling.
2026-09-19 (feat/alarms-live-config, identity at the panel):
+15,792 B on release, +16,912 test, +16,936 test_https,
+15,800 asserts, +1,728 alpha, +6,848 air. CONFIG_VERSION 24: 32
accounts (five until v23), a per-account panel PIN (HMAC-SHA256 chain, 200 rounds,
device-wide salt, looked up BY the PIN), per-sensor alarm actions behind three new
permission bits, a Users item on the panel, five payload codes that carry the acting
user, twelve log codes. The screens (DisplayManager_Users.cpp) and their Core-0 side
(AppManager_Panel.cpp) are TFT-only: the first cut of AppManager_Panel.cpp compiled
into every environment and cost the Air 10,304 B; behind SIMUT_DISPLAY_TFT it costs
6,848 - the migration, the PIN hashing, the CLI and web PIN paths and the wider
account table, all of which every build carries. 72 B of the release delta are the
two follow-ups the rig asked for: Core 1 consuming _repaintSettings before a draw
instead of after it (a Core-0 screen change during a draw was lost, 7 of 7 logins),
and the sensor menu opening on the first row the account may use. Budgets go to
measured + 3,000 (air keeps 1,000); the air .bin is 1,031,212 B, 9,172 under the
OTA ceiling, the release .bin 1,008,300 B, 32,084 under it.
2026-09-19 (feat/alarms-live-config, third commit - the scrambled PIN keypad):
+1,752 B on release, +2,184 test, +2,184 test_https,
+1,744 asserts, +200 alpha, +368 air, measured against the
plain numeric pad the previous commit shipped. Identifying, the ten digits and
two decoys are dealt over four cards, a whole card is one tap and the deal is
rolled again after every tap, so each tap carries its own three glyphs and
Core 0 resolves the tree of strings they can spell (PinKeypad.h,
scramblePinKeys, pinSetMatches). Setting a PIN keeps an ordered pad, a
second small renderer. Most of the delta is the search and the chained digest
that makes it affordable; the imageless builds pay for the chain, for clearing
an account record whole on delete, and for `show display keypad`.
2026-09-19 (feat/alarms-live-config, fourth commit - GET /api/keypad and the
two records that were being filtered): +448 B on release, +368 test, +368
test_https, +456 asserts, 0 alpha, 0 air. No budget is raised; every
environment still sits inside its margin, and the two imageless builds do not
move at all because the route is behind SIMUT_DISPLAY_TFT.
Of the release delta, 368 B are the route itself, measured by building the
same tree with the handler and its registration removed (998,100 vs 998,468);
the other 80 B are log code 311 SEC_PIN_AMBIGUOUS and raising SEC_PIN_OK and
APP_UI_ALARM_SAVED from LOG_INFO to LOG_WARN.
The route earns its bytes on the bench, not on the product: reading the four
scrambled cards over the serial CLI costs 1.2 s per digit against 0.01 s over
HTTP, a 4-digit panel entry 31.1 s against 4.6 s, and an 8-tap entry ran past
the panel's 30 s idle guard - which is what killed the first two full-table
runs, at accounts 18 and 21 of 25. Same measurement for the log: 1.76 s over
the console against 0.15 s for /api/logs, on a log holding 1,189 records.
2026-09-20 (feat/alarms-live-config, identity policy - CONFIG_VERSION 25):
+5,960 B on release, +8,400 test, +5,952 asserts, +1,096 alpha, +2,168 air.
Three things, and they share one header (PinKeypad.h): the account is chosen
BEFORE the PIN (the keypad verifies ONE digest instead of searching 32, which
is what made a blind four-digit entry land on somebody 20.2% of the time with
a full table, and what made two accounts inside one entry refuse both); the
keypad is a policy (1, 2 or 3 glyphs per key, digits or 0-9A-Z) with its
length ceiling derived from CPU - a tap tree costs S^n SHA-256 at 36.6 us a
node, so 3 glyphs stop at 8 taps, 2 at 12 and 1 at 16; and the lockout ladder
is per account with a panel-wide ceiling, because the global-only ladder let
six wrong taps from anybody shut the panel until someone power-cycled it.
Two measurements paid for themselves while this was written. A `sscanf` in
the new CLI handler overflowed the Air's FLASH by 15,404 B on its own -
AppManager_CmdHandlers.cpp already carried the comment saying it pulls
__ssvfscanf_r and that the one it replaced was the last in the image. And
PinKb::GRIDS, a constexpr table at namespace scope, was being copied into
every translation unit that took its address: 128 B x 8 objects, fixed by
`inline constexpr` (the same trap is still open in PasswordKeyboard.h).
pico_w_test_https is the one env that needed room taken from it rather than
found: it is pico_w_test plus BearSSL, it had 5,916 B left before this work,
and it now serves ALARMS_PAGE, FILE_PAGE and TEL_PAGE from LittleFS
(custom_fs_pages, 17,443 B) exactly as the note in pico_w_test says to. The
three must be uploaded to /web/ on the bench unit before a suite runs there.
Budgets go to measured + 3,000 (air keeps its 1,000). Real .bin slack under
the 1,040,384 B OTA ceiling: release 23,924, test 19,132, test_https 11,500,
asserts 21,756, alpha 50,036, air 5,076.
2026-09-20 (same branch, second pass — SIMUT_PANEL_PIN): the panel PIN is
now compiled ONLY into images that have a touch panel. It was never gated:
v24 already shipped the keypad's validator, the digest search, `user pin`,
the web fields and seven display stubs into the Air and the alpha, which
have no screen to prove anything to. Removing it takes the Air 2,750 B and
the alpha 972 B of v25 code, plus what v24 had put there: the Air is now
1,528 B SMALLER than it was on main before this whole branch, and its .bin
is byte-for-byte the size it was there — the identity work costs the
imageless builds nothing.
What deliberately stays in every image is the digest CHAIN (pinChainInit/
Step/Final/pinDigestWith, 254 B): the stored form of a PIN is schema, not
feature. A board flashed with the Air and back to a panel image has to come
back with its PINs, so the Air still seeds the salt on a fresh config and
still converts a v23 displayPin on migration. The config LAYOUT is
unconditional for the same reason — sizeof(SystemConfig) is the schema.
The page is one blob for every image, so it adapts at runtime instead:
/api/config omits pin_min and /api/users omits the `pin` key where there is
no panel, and the page drops the policy row, the PIN column and the PIN
field on their absence. That costs 149 B of gzipped UI in every image and
is what keeps a headless device from offering a setting it would refuse.
Budgets to measured + 3,000 (air 1,000). .bin slack under the OTA ceiling:
release 23,732, test 18,940, test_https 11,308, asserts 21,564,
2026-09-20 (same branch, third pass — identity IS the name): +384 B release,
+256 air, +312 alpha. Two things the rig made obvious.
An alarm record carried the acting user as a SLOT (actor = slot + 1) and the
name was resolved when the payload was built — minutes later, from
cfg.users[actor-1]. The queue waits for the server to confirm and a slot is
reusable, so deleting an account in that window left a queued AUDIT record
signed by whoever took the slot next. The name is now COPIED into the record
at push time (AlarmRecord grew 16 -> 32 B, 2,048 B at the 64-record ceiling)
and never looked up again. The stack paid for it and then some: the send
path had an AlarmRecord tmp[ALARM_QUEUE_MAX] on the STACK that was copied
into a heap vector anyway — 1,024 B of stack removed by snapshotting
straight into the vector, which is also what let the record grow.
Deleting an account now goes through StorageManager::wipeUserAccount( ), a
volatile byte-wise overwrite of the WHOLE record, on all four paths (panel,
web delete, web slot allocation, CLI). v24 cleared only pinHash on the web
allocation path — the symptom that had been found — and left name, password
hash, salt and permission bits for the next account to inherit.
SEC_PIN_OK (308) now carries the account NAME in its text: ctx is an integer
and the slot behind it is reusable, so a log read months later attributed an
action to whoever holds that slot now.
2026-09-20 (same branch, fix): +48 B on the four panel images — the PIN
policy helpers moved from HIST_PAGE into LANG_JS. They had been defined next
to the event dictionary and used in CFG_PAGE and USR_PAGE; each WebUI page is
an independent gz blob, so window.hasPanelPin( ) was undefined there and the
TypeError took down the whole config form. Proven on the device, not deduced:
config.html used it once and defined it zero times, users.html five and zero.
build_webui_gz.py now FAILS the build on that class of defect (a window.foo( )
used in a page that neither defines it nor loads a lang.js that does), which
was verified by removing the definition again and watching the gate name
CFG_PAGE.
2026-09-20 (feat/wifi-scan): +2,776 B on release, +2,784 test, +2,800
test_https, +2,776 asserts, +1,464 alpha, +1,464 air. A scan the network page
can run, including from AP mode, where the SSID has to be typed from memory
today because the radio is serving the page instead of listening to the air.
Of the release delta, 1,103 B are the page itself, measured: the gzipped
NET_PAGE blob goes 2,728 -> 3,831 B, and that same blob is in every image.
The rest is the device side - a scan state machine on NetworkManager that
polls from the TOP of update( ), before the AP-mode early return, so a scan
started while the AP is up is still collected.
The two imageless builds carry 1,312 B LESS of the firmware side than the
panel builds do, which is not explained here: both link the same page blob
and the same NetworkManager. What is measured is the delta; the split is
reported as found, not as understood.
Budgets go to measured + 3,000 across the board, which is the margin every
env in this file is already carrying (the 1,000 the Air notes above asked
for was widened to ~2,992 by the v25 passes and is not narrowed back here).
Real .bin slack under the 1,040,384 B OTA ceiling: release 16,300, test
11,436, test_https 3,804, asserts 14,124, alpha 45,940, air 5,076. Both the
Air and the alpha grew 4,096 B of .bin for 1,464 B of code: their images
crossed one of the 4 KiB .data alignment steps this file describes at the
top, which is why the .bin delta and the 'used' delta disagree here.
pico_w_test_https now trips the gate's WARN at 3,804 B - under one flash
sector. It is the env with the least room (pico_w_test plus BearSSL) and the
next thing added to it has to take a fourth page out to LittleFS, the way
ALARMS_PAGE, FILE_PAGE and TEL_PAGE already went.
2026-09-20 (feat/wifi-scan, follow-up): -16 B on every image and no budget
moves. GET /api/wifi/scan now answers 503 to ANY refusal, instead of falling
back to the finished sweep still sitting in the buffer: `again` asks for a
NEW list, and serving the old one shows networks from minutes ago with
nothing saying so. 'measured' is updated because it has to describe an image
that exists.
2026-09-20 (feat/wifi-scan, the UI pass): +624 B on release, +632 test, +616
test_https, +608 asserts, +8 alpha, +4,096 air. The CONTENT is 601 B and
every image carries the same 601: the NET_PAGE blob goes 3,831 -> 4,339
(+508) and LANG_JS 11,838 -> 11,931 (+93, the two eye symbols in the shared
sprite). Three things: the lock beside a secured SSID and the signal bars
are DRAWN now (sprite icon, CSS bars) instead of written with emoji and
box-drawing characters, which is the rule v2.1.5 set; the scan button is the
height of the field beside it (every input carries `margin: 0 0 16px`, which
sits OUTSIDE its border box, so a flex `stretch` made the button 16 px
taller); and the Wi-Fi password has a reveal button.
The per-environment numbers disagree with the 601 because .rodata is padded
up to a 4 KiB multiple - the linker aligns .data's LOAD address, as the note
at the top of this file says. alpha had slack and shows +8; the Air did not
and its .rodata went 462,848 -> 466,944, a whole page for 601 B of content.
🔴 THE AIR IS NOW 980 B UNDER THE OTA CEILING (1,039,404 B of .bin against
1,040,384). It was 9,172 before this branch and 5,076 after the scan itself.
Two 4 KiB steps in one branch. The next thing added to the Air - any image,
any page, since the web blobs are shared - makes it refuse to update over
the air while `used` still looks 21 kB from the slot ceiling. Giving ~601 B
back anywhere in the Air drops it a whole page and returns 4,096.
pico_w_test_https is 3,212 B under the same ceiling and still warns.
Same day, the same pass, after the gate below found it: two of the tokens
that CSS used did not exist. `--fundo-sutil` and `--tinta-fraca` are not in
either palette (the names are `--superficie-2` and `--tinta-2`), and a
`var( )` with no definition makes the browser drop the whole declaration, so
the scan button had no background and the dBm no secondary colour, in both
themes. Nothing failed: not the compile, not the minifier, not the helper
gate. build_webui_gz.py now refuses the build on it. -16 B, budgets unmoved.
2026-09-21 (feat/web-ui-per-build): -48 B on the four panel builds and
-4,096 on the two without one. The whole web UI was going into every image:
the Air and the alpha carried the panel mirror, the screen capture and the
theme selector - 2,363 B of gzipped page, measured by A/B - talking to four
routes (/api/screen_stream, /api/touch, /api/screenshot, /api/keypad) that
the `#if SIMUT_DISPLAY_TFT` in WebManager_Core.cpp does not even register
there. Buttons that answer 404.
WebUI.h now has `/* @IF tft */ ... /* @ENDIF */` blocks and build_webui_gz.py
cuts them where platformio.ini says `custom_web_omit = tft`. The default is
to omit NOTHING, so an env that forgets the option ships fat, which is the
safe way to be wrong. The cut is in the stamp, beside the layout, or the
second env would be handed the first one's header.
This is NOT the custom_fs_pages diet and the 2026-08-17 rule above still
holds for that one: there the page exists and lives elsewhere, and a missing
file is a runtime error. Here nothing is missing - the control and the route
go together.
Two gates come with it, and both run even when nothing is omitted, or
whoever only builds the release never learns they broke the Air: a function
defined inside a block and called outside it, and an element id that only
exists inside a block and is fetched outside it. Verified by breaking each
one and watching it name the symbol. The second is the one that matters -
`getElementById('themeSel').value =` on a stripped element is a TypeError in
the middle of the refresh loop, which is the shape of the 2026-09-20
hasPanelPin defect.
Real .bin slack under the 1,040,384 B OTA ceiling: air 5,076 (it was 980
before this, one 4 KiB step from refusing an update), alpha 50,036.
Same branch, the fix the maintainer found on the device: +24 B on the four
panel builds, 0 on the two without one. Moving the panel UI behind @IF took
loadThemes( ) out of the DOMContentLoaded that both images share - it would
have dangled there - and it was never put back INSIDE the block. The theme
selector sat on 'Loading...' forever, in the image WITH a panel. The gate
did not see it: it asked whether a block's function was called from OUTSIDE,
never whether it was called at all. It asks both now, and it counts
references in CODE - the first attempt was defeated by the comment naming
loadThemes( ), the same way --espaco-N defeated the CSS-token gate.
Same branch, the topbar on a phone: +72 B on the four panel builds, 0 on the
two without one (their .rodata padding swallowed it - they have a whole page
of slack now). The IP in the top-right corner was the ONLY item in that bar
that could shrink, so on a 360 px screen it rendered as '192.168.3…'. It is
also the only information there - which device am I on. The status pill no
longer shrinks, the brand's suffix is hidden below 640 px, and the version
it used to carry moved into the drawer, where a phone can still reach it.
2026-09-21 (fix/license-consistency): +8 B on the four panel builds, 0 on
the two without one. The /license page said Copyright 2025 while the LICENSE
file, the firmware string and both language packs said 2026; the page is the
copy a user reads. tools/check_license.py keeps the five copies agreeing and
checks that both release scripts ship the file - build_release.sh packaged
the whole source tree into the Arduino IDE zips without it, which is the one
artefact the MIT text's own 'all copies' clause was not being honoured in.
2026-09-22 (fix/ap-mode-reachable, v2.7.1): measured against main at 994f058.
'used' +1,424 B on release, +1,440 test, +1,464 test_https, +1,424 asserts,
+5,160 alpha, +224 air. Only the ALPHA budget is raised, and this is the raise
the rule asks to be argued for.
Per SECTION, which is where the alpha's number comes apart: .text +1,304
release, +1,064 alpha, +224 air; .rodata +120 release, 0 air - and +4,096 on
the alpha, which is ONE ALIGNMENT STEP and not content. main's alpha .rodata is
442,368 B, exactly 108 pages of 4 KiB with zero slack, so the first byte added
to it costs a whole page. The alpha's real cost here is 1,064 B of code.
Budget: alpha 978,396 -> 983,396 (measured + 3,000, the margin this file
carries). Every other environment stays where it was and is still inside its

.bin deltas: +1,424 / +1,440 / +1,464 / +1,424 on the four panel builds,
+4,096 on the alpha (the same page) and ZERO on the Air - its 224 B of .text
fit in padding it already had. Real .bin slack under the 1,040,384 B OTA
ceiling: release 14,028, test 9,132, test_https 1,500, asserts 11,852,
alpha 45,940, air 5,076 (unchanged).
pico_w_test_https keeps warning and is now 1,500 B from the ceiling, its
tightest yet. It is the bench HTTPS image, not a field one - release-ota.yml
does not publish it - but the next thing added to the panel builds has to take
a fourth page out to LittleFS, as the 2026-09-20 note already said.
What the bytes bought, in the order they were found:
- beginAP( ) waits out a scan already issued to the driver before taking the
radio, and READS softAP( )'s return. Without it, an AP raised while the
station was hunting for an SSID that is not there was visible at 94% and
unjoinable - 45 s and a timeout, twice, against 4,07 s after the fix. That
is the state the new fallback fires in, so this is what makes it work.
- the AP-by-touch window moved to after startCore1( ) AND after Core 1 has
painted a frame (measured on main: window [3919..7419] ms, Core 1 launched
at 7457 - the prompt reached the glass 38 ms after the last moment a finger
could start the gesture; measured here: first frame 4667, window
- the alpha's LCD publishes the SSID and the key, which reached no display on
that build at all, and the TFT keeps them on its last boot screen instead of
scrolling them out of the five-slot ring.
- a twelfth settings row that starts the setup AP behind a confirmation.
- an automatic fallback for an unconfigured device or one that cannot get on
its network. Air is excluded from both, which is why it pays 224 B.
Also here: _menuItems was 10 entries against an 11-entry table since v25, so
an account holding every bit wrote one past the end of it - shown on the rig
as an admin menu with ten rows and no numbers.
